subject: gk
question: The structures of temples located in India are classified as phamsana and latina on the basis of which of their parts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shikhara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The classification of temple structures into phamsana and latina styles is based on the design of the **Shikhara**.
 
• **Phamsana** temples generally have a broader base and a gradual incline, resembling a pyramid-like structure.
 
• **Latina** temples have a more curvilinear and vertical rising Shikhara, often resembling a beehive shape.
 
• These classifications are primarily found in North Indian temple architecture, specifically in the Nagara style.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Garbagriha:**

 
 
• The Garbagriha, or sanctum sanctorum, is the innermost chamber of a temple where the main deity is enshrined.
 
• It is the most sacred part of the temple and is usually located directly under the Shikhara.
 
 
 
• **Amalaka:**
 
 
• An Amalaka is a stone disk, often ribbed, placed atop the Shikhara.
 
• It symbolizes the fruit of the amla tree and represents the sun.
 
 
 
• **Mandap:**
 
 
• The Mandap is a pavilion or hall, often used for public rituals and ceremonies.
 
• It is typically located in front of the Garbagriha and may be open or enclosed.
 
 
 
• **Nagara Style:**
 
 
• The Nagara style is a distinct form of North Indian temple architecture characterized by its towering Shikharas.
 
• It contrasts with the Dravidian style found in South India, which features pyramidal towers and intricate sculptures.
